I've completed analysis of all 4 sensitive samples, and the 0.9 value they produce does not align with the observed 0.6 result. I've ruled out several potential causes including label matching issues, score calculation logic, and reference data access problems, and will next check relevant threshold binarization rules using the four sensitive samples with a threshold lower than 0.5.

I've sorted out the high-dose value data of the four sensitive samples, and preliminarily confirmed that the threshold binarization rule is executed before headline processing. Next, I will further verify the cause of the 0.6 result.

After ruling out several invalid hypotheses, I've preliminarily confirmed that the headline threshold binarization rule uses the ">" operator to match the score.

I tested multiple rule adjustment schemes and found existing binarization rules cannot correctly process categorical score data. I will unify all scores to raw viability values and use source replicate means of 10 relevant drugs at corresponding doses as standard labels. I have preliminarily verified that the previously assumed 0.5 threshold is inconsistent with the actual situation for some resistance cases.

I've verified the high-dose viability values of multiple samples, confirming that using the ">" operator with a 0.5 threshold for categorical scores can resolve the earlier prediction mismatch, as the original "==" operator failed to match boolean logic and caused all 4 sensitive samples to be misjudged.

I've confirmed LC133's score threshold settings.
